Subject: Follow-up: Deployment mode & EU/APAC data residency (NordBank)

Hi Sara - thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment:

- Requirement recap: NordBank needs strong EU data residency guarantees for customer PII and audit logs; potential APAC presence for upcoming Asia initiative.
- Deployment modes under consideration: Hosted API (Redwood hosted in EU), Dedicated (reserved EU capacity), Private (VPC or on-prem for full control).
- Primary constraints: data residency for logs and model inputs, cross-region routing for low-latency APAC users, and SOC2/audit evidence for procurement.

Next steps I promised on the call:
1) Share a short matrix comparing Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for EU/APAC (latency, guarantees, timeline). Attachment: deployment-options-overview.pdf
2) Confirm which artifacts you need for procurement (SOC2 snapshot, network diagrams) - I attached SOC2 snapshot.
3) Internal: I'll loop in our deployments team to confirm EU region capacity and APAC edge routing options.

Could you confirm whether NordBank requires logs to be stored exclusively in EU-controlled storage (yes/no), and whether you can list any specific APAC regions (e.g., singapore, tokyo) you expect to prioritize? That will help us scope Dedicated vs Private.

Thanks - happy to jump on a short follow-up if helpful.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Hi Aditya - thanks for the summary and the attachments. Quick answers:

- Yes - logs and any persisted PII must remain in the EU. We cannot have backups or audit logs replicated outside the EU without explicit legal review.
- APAC priority regions: primarily Singapore (asia-southeast1) for the first phase, Tokyo for later expansion.
- For procurement: SOC2 snapshot is good; we will also ask for data flow diagrams and an expected SLA for Dedicated capacity.

We are hoping to decide on a preferred deployment path by end of Q2. For now, we want to understand whether Redwood Hosted in EU can provide the "logs-in-EU-only" guarantee and what cross-region routing looks like for Singapore users (edge vs cross-region calls).

Thanks,
Sara Johansson

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Sara Johansson <sara.johansson@nordbank.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 16:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Deployment mode & EU/APAC data-residency (NordBank)

Hi all - thanks for the clear ask, Sara. Short answers and recommended next steps below:

1) Logs-in-EU-only for Hosted API: Yes - we can configure Redwood Hosted (EU region) so that all persisted logs, audit trails, and backups are written to EU-only storage buckets and are not replicated. Implementation notes: write-after-receive pipeline writes logs to customer-scoped EU buckets; cross-region backups are disabled for EU tenants by default when the tenancy is marked as EU-residency. We will provide a data flow diagram for procurement. (See attached soc2-snapshot.pdf for compliance posture.)

2) APAC routing for Singapore users: If you choose Hosted EU, Singapore users will have cross-region calls to EU and typical observed RTTs range 180-260ms depending on ISP; we offer an optional edge proxy that terminates TLS locally in Singapore and forwards requests to EU while still ensuring persistent storage remains in EU. The edge proxy reduces perceived connection time (TLS handshake) but does not eliminate cross-region RTT for token streaming. If NordBank needs sub-120ms P95 for interactive UI, Dedicated capacity in APAC or Private deployment with an APAC presence is recommended.

3) Recommended path: Given procurement wants logs strictly in EU, Hosted EU is acceptable (we can lock logs to EU). However if NordBank requires guaranteed APAC low-latency for production users, propose either Dedicated reserved capacity in APAC (we can provision a dedicated pool in singapore-region; typical lead time 6-10 weeks depending on commit) or Private VPC (on-prem or VPC) for full control and local data egress. Private has longer onboarding (8-14 weeks) but provides maximum control.

Action items:
- Aditya: I'll prepare a short data flow diagram + a one-page Hosted-vs-Dedicated-vs-Private matrix for procurement.
- Sara: If possible, confirm whether a 6-10 week lead time for Dedicated in SG fits your timeline, or if Private/on-prem is mandated by procurement.

Happy to schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive with NordBank IT compliance next week if useful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference
